context:
Treat current adapter-mixin execution as the likely production path, but prove
it before changing docs. Separate lifecycle cleanup from result-bundle parity
so old-runner decisions do not block the most important contract test.
description:
Production DataFrame execution appears to route through adapter.run_benchmark
and the DataFrame benchmark mixin. The older core/runner/dataframe_runner.py
still exists, is documented like a live runner, and has tests. The sharper
architectural risk is not that production has three canonical paths; it is
that an old path has unclear lifecycle status and no real exported-bundle
SQL-vs-DataFrame contract guards the result boundary.

This item classifies dataframe_runner.py as supported, internal compatibility,
or deprecated, then adds one real SQL-vs-DataFrame exported-result bundle
contract test.

work_units.notes:
Decision: `benchbox/core/runner/dataframe_runner.py` is a deprecated
internal compatibility runner. Production DataFrame execution is the
adapter-mixin path:
`run_benchmark_lifecycle()` -> `adapter.run_benchmark()` ->
`BenchmarkExecutionMixin.run_benchmark()`.

Production behavior tests are DataFrame mixin/adapter lifecycle tests and
exported bundle parity. `tests/unit/core/runner/test_dataframe_runner.py`
and `tests/unit/core/runner/test_dataframe_runner_lifecycle.py` are
compatibility tests for the deprecated standalone runner.

Choose exactly one status and record it in
docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md and docs/reference/public-contracts.md:
  - supported public/internal runner,
  - internal compatibility shim,
  - deprecated compatibility fossil,
  - removed after one beta window.

The decision must identify which tests are production behavior tests and
which are compatibility tests.

Added module lifecycle constants and docstring guidance to
`benchbox/core/runner/dataframe_runner.py`, registered the lifecycle in
`docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md`, and updated
`docs/reference/public-contracts.md` plus
`docs/design/architecture.md` to direct production DataFrame execution to
`adapter.run_benchmark()` and `BenchmarkExecutionMixin`.

If w1 chooses deprecation or compatibility fossil: update docs so
DataFrame execution is described through adapter.run_benchmark and the
DataFrame benchmark mixin. Keep only narrow compatibility tests for
dataframe_runner.py until the removal window ends.

Do not delete the runner in the same change unless the compatibility
registry says the removal window is already closed.

If w1 chooses supported/internal runner: dataframe_runner.py should
delegate to the same adapter-mixin production path or share a lower-level
helper so field population cannot drift.

Avoid maintaining a separate result-construction path unless a contract
test proves the divergence is intentional.

work_units.notes:
Added `test_exported_sql_and_dataframe_bundles_share_cross_mode_contract`
in `tests/unit/core/results/test_result_parity.py`. The test creates a
SQL result through a concrete `PlatformAdapter.run_benchmark()` path,
creates a DataFrame result through `BenchmarkExecutionMixin.run_benchmark()`,
exports both through `ResultExporter`, reloads the JSON payloads, and
compares schema version, benchmark/config identity, phases, query IDs,
rows, validation, errors, execution metadata keys, and timing field
names/units without comparing exact timing values.

Pick the smallest reliable benchmark/platform pair available in fast or
focused integration tests. Compare exported bundle fields, not synthetic
dataclass construction alone.

Required invariants:
  - schema version,
  - benchmark/config identity,
  - phase presence and skipped/not-run semantics,
  - query IDs,
  - row counts when available,
  - validation state,
  - error fields,
  - execution metadata keys,
  - timing field names and units.

Do not assert exact timing values.
